subject: Air-gapped deployment discovery — HelixBio next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@helixbio.com>, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@helixbio.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Air-gapped deployment discovery — HelixBio next steps

Hi Aaron / Samantha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side plus action items so we keep momentum on the private (air-gapped) deployment conversation: 

Summary of what we heard
- Requirement: fully air-gapped inference for selected genomics pipeline (no egress from the compute network).
- Preference: on-prem appliance with customer-managed key store (HSM/KMS integration later).
- Concern: firmware and security-patch process, and how upgrades are delivered while maintaining offline posture.

Open questions we need to confirm (see next steps):
1) Confirm preferred maintenance window (weekday overnight vs weekend).
2) Provide the network VLAN/subnet diagram (we discussed you sending a redacted version).
3) Clarify storage encryption — will HelixBio manage disk-level encryption keys or should Redwood provide sealed image + key wrap guidance?
4) Are there any procurement constraints on accepting on-site spare parts or retained hardware?

Attachments: I’ve attached a site-readiness checklist and a short privacy note. Rishi / Neha, can you weigh in on the upgrade path and any hard blockers for offline patch distribution?

Next steps / owners
- Aaron: send redacted network diagram and confirm maintenance window (by EOD Wed).
- Marissa: coordinate follow-up call with Redwood infra (I’ll include Rishi).
- Rishi/Neha: provide a short MOP (maintenance/upgrade) summary and list of required spare parts.

Proposed dates for a technical preflight call: Thu Aug 6 or Fri Aug 7 (30–45 minutes). Let me know which works.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: site-readiness-checklist.pdf, redwood-privacy-note.txt

From: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@helixbio.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@helixbio.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment discovery — HelixBio next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap. A few quick answers and clarifications from our side: 

- Network diagram: attaching a redacted PNG (see helix-network-diagram.png). The appliance will live on VLAN 120, behind our internal firewall; all outbound ports are blocked except for management over an intermediary jump host during scheduled maintenance.

- Maintenance window: We prefer Sunday 02:00–05:00 local time for firmware/patch work to minimize pipeline disruptions.

- Storage encryption: Helix currently manages full-disk encryption via their internal KMS (key material never leaves HSM). For the initial deployment we’d like Redwood to support sealed image boot and provide guidance for key wrap so we can retain control.

- Spare parts: We can accept on-site replacement blades under our asset intake process but cannot retain Redwood-owned spare hardware on-site.

Questions for the Redwood team: 
1) How do you handle rollbacks if a firmware push causes service degradation in an air-gapped setup? Do you provide signed rollbacks packaged in the same air-gap artifact?
2) Can you outline the telemetry you need for health checks if we must limit outbound telemetry to a narrow set of management endpoints?

I’ve attached the diagram and a short redacted service boundary doc. Happy to join the technical preflight on Thu Aug 6 at 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Aaron Liu
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, HelixBio
aaron.liu@helixbio.com

Attachments: helix-network-diagram.png

Rishi / Neha —

Forwarding Aaron’s responses. Key asks from Helix: Sunday maintenance window, sealed-image + key-wrap flow, no on-site Redwood spare retention.

Can you draft a concise MOP we can share on the call (2–3 bullets each):
- Upgrade/rollback strategy for air-gapped firmware and model updates
- Minimal telemetry and health-check endpoints with data classification (what we store locally, what we allow outbound)
- Recommended spare parts list and a procurement-friendly statement that we won’t require retention of Redwood-owned spare hardware at customer site

I’ll book Thu Aug 6 10:00 PT for the preflight and include Aaron / Samantha.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@helixbio.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Aug 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Air-gapped deployment discovery — HelixBio next steps

Aaron / Marissa —

Thanks for the diagram and the clear asks. High-level answers below; I’ll bring the detailed MOP to the preflight call Thursday.

1) Firmware/model upgrades & rollback- We deliver upgrades as signed, versioned artifacts that can be transferred via removable media or a secured jump host. Each artifact includes a signed rollback bundle (previous image + signature) so you can revert to the last known-good state without external fetch. Rollbacks are performed offline using our CLI tool and require local ops creds and an audit token that your HSM can validate.

2) Telemetry & health checks- Minimal approach: local metrics + event logs retained on-device; health-check ping allowed only to a management relay (jump host) that you operate. We can restrict outbound ports to a single TLS endpoint and provide a audited handshake protocol. No telemetry leaves the air-gapped boundary without an explicit signed release.

3) Spare parts / procurement- Recommended spares: 2x NVMe hot-swap blades, 1x power supply N+1, and 1x GPU mezzanine replacement. We are fine with Helix receiving replacement parts and performing on-site swap under your asset retention policy — Redwood retains ownership of the replacement units but will not require on-site storage of deep spares. We can ship on-call RMAs under an SLA-backed process.

Operational next steps before the preflight call:
- Marissa: confirm final attendee list and share the Drive link to the site readiness doc.
- Aaron: confirm Sunday 02:00–05:00 maintenance window (if agreed we’ll bake into the MOP).
- Neha: prepare the short checklist for verification steps we’ll do during the first maintenance (signature verification, local integrity checks, and rollback drill).

I’ll join Thu Aug 6 10:00 PT. If anything changes ping me directly.

—Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
